# How Pages lays out fonts of the Mac, as measured on the reference
# machine (DOC-05). Desk lays a family out this way whatever font stands
# for it, so its lines are as tall and as wide as in Pages.
# ascent, descent and leading are in ems: the leading is the space added
# to each line. "above" puts the leading over the text, as Pages does with
# Apple's own fonts, which have no line gap: their leading is a fifth of
# their height. "below" puts it under the text, as with fonts that have a
# line gap of their own. "fi fl" means Pages joins fi and fl into
# ligatures, and no others, as in Times and Palatino, which have only those
# two (Courier, fixed in width, has none);
# "none" means it joins nothing. data/fonts/README.md explains.
